verdict.rationale: YPOG publishes a dedicated briefing on how seedstrapping affects convertible loan agreements, SAFEs and ASAs, covering governance and valuation-cap risks and when a priced round is the better choice. It frames these instruments as the default for pre-seed and seed financing, and its transactions practice claims advice 'from inception to exit'. This is a single first-party explainer rather than documented deep, repeated practice. missing for 10: downloadable SAFE/CLA templates or forms, an explicitly stated pre-seed/seed convertible financing practice or deal track record, multiple in-depth explainers, independent corroboration of the firm's convertible-instrument experience.

support.subject: As a founder, the firm documents deep experience with SAFEs and convertible instruments for pre-seed and seed rounds — published explainers, forms, or a stated early-stage financing practice

citations.quote: This briefing explains how seedstrapping affects convertible loan agreements (CLAs), SAFEs and advance subscription agreements (ASAs), where governance and valuation cap risks arise, and when a priced equity round is the better structure.
Convertible loan agreements (CLAs), SAFEs, and related instruments such as the UK's Advance Subscription Agreements (ASAs) have become the default for pre-seed and seed financing across Europe.
Well advised from inception to exit.
